title: Run an agent incident containment drill
description: Select an incident, choose how broadly to stop authority, and set a recovery gate. The timeline exposes ongoing reach, evidence quality, availability cost, and recurrence risk.

containmentScopes.label: Pause this run
containmentScopes.detail: Stop the active loop but leave sibling runs, delegated credentials, and shared context available.

containmentScopes.label: Contain the principal
containmentScopes.detail: Pause all runs for the agent identity, revoke delegated tokens, and quarantine its context namespace.

containmentScopes.label: Quarantine the tenant
containmentScopes.detail: Block agent execution and risky tools across the tenant while responders investigate shared context or credentials.

recoveryPlans.label: Restart immediately
recoveryPlans.detail: Create a fresh process without preserving evidence, reconciling effects, rotating credentials, or cleaning context.

recoveryPlans.label: Reconcile and rotate
recoveryPlans.detail: Preserve the trajectory, inventory external effects, rotate credentials, repair the control, and resume at bounded scope.

recoveryPlans.label: Clean-state canary
recoveryPlans.detail: Preserve evidence, reconcile effects, rotate credentials, remove poisoned state, and verify a low-risk canary before restoring authority.

incidents.label: Poisoned payables memory
incidents.brief: A false payment instruction persists in a tenant-shared memory namespace and has influenced several scheduled runs.
incidents.signal: Three agents propose the same unapproved bank destination after reading one shared memory item.
incidents.containmentReason: The influence and credentials cross agent identities inside one tenant, so stopping one run or principal leaves active paths.
incidents.recoveryReason: External payments must be reconciled and the shared memory must be removed before a clean canary can prove the path is safe.
incidents.userConsequence: Duplicate or attacker-directed payments can continue from sibling agents until tenant-scoped authority and shared memory are contained.

incidents.label: Sensitive-data webhook chain
incidents.brief: One support agent read private customer records and posted them to an unapproved webhook using a live delegated token.
incidents.signal: A private-data read is followed by unusual public egress from the same principal.
incidents.containmentReason: The active credential and sibling runs belong to one principal; tenant-wide shutdown is safe but unnecessarily disruptive.
incidents.recoveryReason: Preserve the chain, rotate the credential, identify every transmitted record, repair egress policy, and verify a bounded canary.
incidents.userConsequence: More customer records may leave the system while the principal's token remains valid, and affected users cannot be identified without trajectory evidence.

incidents.label: Runaway deployment loop
incidents.brief: A deployment agent retries an ambiguous timeout and creates overlapping production rollouts with the same credential.
incidents.signal: Write rate and retry count exceed the trajectory budget while deployment completion remains unknown.
incidents.containmentReason: All runs using the deployer identity must stop so another retry cannot race with investigation.
incidents.recoveryReason: Compare the deployment system of record with trajectory events, rotate the token, repair idempotency, and canary one known artifact.
incidents.userConsequence: Overlapping rollouts can create inconsistent production state or an outage even if the agent eventually reports success.

incidents.label: Rogue multi-agent coordinator
incidents.brief: A coordinator delegates a modified goal to several tenant workers and uses shared service credentials and context.
incidents.signal: Multiple worker agents begin unrelated high-risk actions after one coordinator message.
incidents.containmentReason: The coordinator, shared credentials, and worker context create several active principals, so containment must cover the tenant boundary.
incidents.recoveryReason: Reconstruct delegated tasks, rotate shared identity, remove poisoned coordination state, reconcile effects, and restart from a signed goal envelope.
incidents.userConsequence: Unrelated tools and resources remain exposed while any worker can continue the coordinator's modified objective.
